checks: The exact base projection is [0,1] and both measured rectangles are prescribed at its exposed endpoints. Their areas are 4L and 2L. The accepted exposed-fiber formula applies to all marks. Central symmetry gives half area at each rectangle center, and opposite continuous cuts bound every other point by half area. Thus the maximum raw depth is 2L and the normalization is 6L.

At z=0 both oblique cuts take half of A. At z=1 the first takes only the x=−1 edge of B and the second only the x=−2 edge. These boundary traces have zero planar area, so both raw masses are exactly 2L.

The convex-hull sections are Minkowski interpolants of the two rectangles. The thresholds −z and −2z retain horizontal widths L(1−z) on their respective sides throughout the real projection. Multiplying by the common height 2(1−z)+2Lz and integrating gives cap volume L(L+2)/3. For the entire body the width is 2L(1−z)+z, giving volume (2L²+6L+1)/3.

Subtracting one third from the ambient fraction gives (L²−1)/(3(2L²+6L+1))>0. Substitution L=2 gives 8/21 and the gap 1/21. Continuous normals are opposite and balance with equal positive coefficients. Original §3 uses exactly these two closed caps and the same ratios.

dependencies.hypotheses: There are exactly two positive integer bases and each is strictly exposed by a choice of sign of the linear base coordinate. The theorem identifies their raw mixed depths with ordinary rectangle depths at every mark.

overlap.comparison: The accepted exposed-fiber theorem computes the pointwise mixed depth needed for the construction, but does not compare these oblique caps against ambient volume. The negative sampling discrepancy is additional.

readability: The signed correction here is original mixed fraction minus ambient fraction. Its negative sign follows from the displayed positive gap in the reverse order.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Both caps are actual oblique minimizers at a globally deepest mark of the canonical hull and have strictly larger ambient than original mixed fractions.
